answer:
Marked text (bold + numbered = oral continuation phenomenon):

Parachutes are big, heavy and bulky. Typical parachutes wouldn’t fit beneath your plane seat. They would take up a lot of real estate on the plane and add to its overall weight. **[[1]] To tackle that,** parachutes would be have to be made significantly smaller. **[[2]] Plus** there would have to be systems in place to ensure that the parachute opens only when the passenger is ready to deploy it, and that they work seamlessly every time. All of these factors add to the overall cost of a single flight **[[3]] which needless to say** the passengers would have to bear. **[[4]] As a result,** ticket prices would soar **[[5]] and that’s just bad news for the airline businesses**. **[[6]] As such,** money becomes a major deterrent for having parachutes on board airplanes. **[[7]] It’s important to realize that** when the engines of a plane fail mid flight, the plane doesn’t just drop out of the sky like a stone, it still has the ability to glide. **[[8]] Something that pilots use to execute an emergency landing when something goes wrong.**

**[[9]] All in all,** **[[10]] it’s safe to say that** if something goes wrong during a flight, passengers are safer if they remain strapped to their seats while the pilots attempt an emergency landing rather than jumping out of the plane at 40,000 feet.

| No. | Marked expression | Type / function |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **To tackle that** | Anaphoric purpose transition |
| 2 | **Plus** | Informal additive discourse marker |
| 3 | **which needless to say** | Appended relative clause with parenthetical comment |
| 4 | **As a result** | Resultive discourse marker |
| 5 | **and that’s just bad news for the airline businesses** | Evaluative comment/tail |
| 6 | **As such** | Inferential discourse marker |
| 7 | **It’s important to realize that** | Metadiscursive attention frame |
| 8 | **Something that pilots use to execute an emergency landing when something goes wrong** | Afterthought/appendage fragment |
| 9 | **All in all** | Summative discourse marker |
| 10 | **it’s safe to say that** | Concluding/hedging frame |

Ordinary sentence-internal coordination and subordination — e.g. “and add to its overall weight,” “and that they work seamlessly every time,” “when the engines fail,” “while the pilots attempt,” “rather than jumping” — are not marked because they are grammatical links rather than discourse-level continuation devices.
